description: Warm, cheap for a northern city, and on everyone's list. The first morning you wake up somewhere that is not where you live is worth most of what it cost to get there.
The weeks before going to Lisbon are their own good thing. Kumar, Killingsworth and Gilovich found anticipation of an experience is pleasurable in itself and, notably, unrelated to what it cost.
energy_note: The waiting is part of the thing, not a delay before it.
notes: Waiting for Merlot: anticipatory consumption of experiential and material purchases.

description: Asked years later what made the trip to Lisbon good, people name the company rather than the content. The Harvard Study of Adult Development has been producing that result for eighty-seven years.
notes: Harvard Study of Adult Development: relationship quality is the strongest single predictor of health and happiness.

aspect: What it takes to be allowed
description: A visa application, a set of documents assembled over weeks, a fee that is not returned if the answer is no, and a border officer who is not obliged to admit you.
energy_note: The journey starts months before the journey.
notes: Pairs with the VIS / BOR / AIR categories in assets/text/{iran,nigeria} and MOV / BOR in assets/text/palestine.

description: The trip to lisbon stops being an event and becomes a reference point - retold, compared against, and eventually shorthand inside one family for a whole kind of day.
energy_note: It turns into the story about it.
notes: Experiential purchases retain value through memory where material ones decay; people are markedly unwilling to trade the memory away.

aspect: The one that cannot wait for a decision
description: A funeral happens within days. A visa takes weeks. This is the single most common way the two halves of this game collide, and it resolves the same way almost every time: watching it on a phone held up by a cousin at the graveside.
energy_note: Burying someone by video, because the appointment was in March.
